places.name: Teide National Park
places.intro: The high crater floor of Las Cañadas around Mount Teide, an hour or so by road from the coastal resorts of Tenerife.
facts: Teide National Park holds Starlight certification both as a tourist destination and as a reserve.
The Teide Observatory, run by the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias, sits at about 2,390 m in the park.
Canary Islands law has protected the sky over the observatories from light pollution since 1988.
Low clouds usually form below a temperature inversion that sits well under the peaks, so the park can be clear when the coast is cloudy.
places.tip: It is cold at night up here even in summer. Bring warm layers, and check the road and weather before you drive up.
sources: Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias, observatories leaflet

places.name: La Palma
places.intro: The island of La Palma, home of the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on its highest ridge.
facts: The Roque de los Muchachos Observatory stands at about 2,396 m.
The Canary Islands’ ‘Sky Law’, approved in 1988, limits light pollution to protect the observatories.
As on Tenerife, low clouds generally stay well below the summit ridge.
places.tip: The summit road is long and winding. Allow plenty of time, and do not drive it for the first time in the dark if you can avoid it.
sources: Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias, observatories leaflet

places.name: Atacama Desert
places.region: near San Pedro de Atacama, Chile
places.intro: The high desert of northern Chile around San Pedro de Atacama, the base for most stargazing trips in the region.
facts: The European Southern Observatory calls the Atacama one of the driest places on Earth, with over 300 clear nights a year.
Several of the world’s major observatories are in northern Chile, including ESO’s Paranal and La Silla sites and ALMA.
It is in the southern hemisphere, so the centre of the Milky Way passes high overhead in the southern winter.
places.tip: Plan more than one night. A local operator in San Pedro warns that coming for a single night is risky, and advises avoiding the full Moon.
sources: San Pedro de Atacama Celestial Explorations, the astronomical Chile

places.name: NamibRand Nature Reserve
places.intro: A private nature reserve in the south-west Namib Desert, with lodges and camps rather than towns.
facts: It was named an International Dark Sky Reserve in 2012, the first in Africa.
It holds Gold Tier status, the darkest and strictest category.
places.tip: There is no town nearby, so the sky is dark from horizon to horizon. Stays are at lodges and camps inside or next to the reserve.

places.name: Aoraki Mackenzie
places.region: Lake Tekapo, South Island, New Zealand
places.intro: The Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve on New Zealand’s South Island, with Lake Tekapo as its main base.
facts: The reserve covers over 4,300 km² and holds Gold Tier status.
Lake Tekapo is its stargazing hub.
places.tip: Being far south, winter nights from May to August are long and cold. Summer nights are short.
sources: Dark Sky Project, Dark Sky Reserve NZ
